purpose: Eight independent visual mockups for Biologue; exploration only, no application changes.

concepts.name: Journal
concepts.summary: Editorial pages, quiet rules, actions attached to the work.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-fidelity, plausibly shippable desktop UI design for Biologue, an open-source scientific thinking partner used by biologists. It should look like an original professional product with a strong design point of view. This is an actual working screen, not a landing page, branding board, device photo, or collage. Render a crisp, large landscape image, approximately 16:10, straight-on and filling the frame, with readable typography.

Keep this spatial arrangement so concepts can be compared: conversation at left (about 27% width); a larger editable Python script in the center (about 45% width) with a compact console beneath; research notes and live objects in the upper right, a scientific figure in the lower right (about 28% width). All five areas visible at once. Preserve the working layout but invent the pane chrome, navigation and placement of actions according to this direction. No conventional IDE activity bar, no file-tab strips, no minimap, no VS Code or Positron styling. Avoid copying a typical IDE shell with new colors. Most of the screen is useful content.

Same modest scientific content in every concept: product name exactly "biologue"; project "Macrophage morphology". Left conversation has scientist: "Could this be a batch effect?" and Biologue: "Were treated and control samples imaged on both days?" with a small message composer. Central document is "analysis.py" and shows 10–14 lines of legible Python, including "import pandas as pd", "summary = measurements.groupby(['batch', 'condition']).agg(", "    mean_area=('area', 'mean'),", "    cells=('area', 'size'),", ")" and "print(summary)". Console shows a small neat 4-row output table. Right notes: "Question", "Does treatment change cell shape?", "Observed", "Two experiments on different days.", "Assumption", "Imaging exposure may differ." Show compact objects "measurements", "summary", "24 rows". Figure is a restrained scientific dot plot, title "Cell area by batch", two groups "Day 1" and "Day 2", with a small caption "Illustrative data" and "View source". No claim that a treatment effect has been established. Include functional actions "Run script", "Save", "Inspect" and "Send" where the particular direction specifies. Make the dialogue and notes feel as important as the code. Text and spacing must be clean; no ornamental pseudo controls, no giant decorative science graphics, no fake collaboration avatars, no fabricated advanced features. Use generous but productive spacing, fine typographic hierarchy, and mostly text-labeled actions.

Direction 01 — JOURNAL. A contemporary scientific journal reimagined as a working app. Warm ivory #f8f5ee, near-black ink, dark oxblood accent used only for one active action. Sophisticated large editorial serif section headings, restrained sans UI labels, clean monospaced code. NO boxed cards and NO colored application header. A low, elegant masthead: small serif biologue at far left, project name centered, simple text navigation "Workspace · Context · Agent" at upper right. Panes feel like adjacent columns on one expansive sheet, divided only by thin vertical hairlines and ample margins; each heading lives in the content, not a toolbar. Conversation is a letter-like transcript with names and thin paragraph rules, no bubbles. Script looks like a typeset code document. A small oxblood "Run script →" button sits immediately beneath the final code line, alongside a quiet "Save" link; the console is an inset footnote band below. Notes are marginalia with fine labels. Plot is an unboxed publication figure. "Inspect" is an inline link beside the object count. The composer is an understated underlined writing area with "Send →" at its lower right. Serious, literary, beautiful, entirely digital and crisp: no aged paper texture or illustrations.

Square corners, precise alignment, functional labels, no pill-card SaaS look, no IDE header or tabs. Slim header with bold lowercase biologue and the experiment title; a tiny "PYTHON / READY" status readout sits at upper right. Each spatial pane has a small engraved-style number and upper-left label: "01 DIALOGUE", "02 SCRIPT", "03 CONTEXT", "04 OUTPUT", "05 FIGURE". Every control must serve a real function; no decorative dials, knobs, gauges or switches. Calm, high quality, trustworthy hardware translated into flat software.

No persistent top application toolbar: put the biologue wordmark and project identity in a generous left-column masthead above the conversation. Restrained, warm, sophisticated, extremely readable, no decoration or invented features.

concepts.summary: A shared worktable, labeled cards, and a bottom navigation dock.

Five generously rounded white work cards arranged in the requested stable pane layout, with clear breathing room and subtle depth, NO conventional docked panel bars or tiny tab strips. Restrained indigo and warm amber accents, dark navy typography, friendly but sober humanist sans. Thin header only shows biologue and "Macrophage morphology", with a simple project menu. The conversation card has the heading "Think together" with elegant restrained speech cards, not a social chat clone. Central "analysis.py" card has a large unobtrusive filename, code, and its "Run script" button in the LOWER LEFT of the card, with a plain Save action alongside. Console is a separate low card underneath. Upper-right research card contains carefully separated question, observation, assumption text, plus a compact object list. Lower-right figure is a clean white card with content-first plotting and its controls in the caption. MAIN NAVIGATION is a compact floating horizontal dock centered along the bottom of the window, with clearly labeled destinations "Conversation", "Script", "Objects", "Figures", "Context", "Agent"; use simple line glyphs plus words. Chat composer is integrated at the bottom of the conversation card. No avatars, no sticky-note clutter, no connecting spaghetti arrows, no fake multiplayer UI. Collegial, useful, distinctive, practical.

Panes form one connected continuous ruled grid, with clear 1px and occasional 2px black lines marking hierarchy. Put section labels in slender left MARGINS of each region, e.g. a prominent "01" and "DIALOGUE", "02" and "SCRIPT", etc., and let their content begin inset beneath. The figure is a publication graph without a card, red and black marks. Right notes use a two-column label/value structure, objects a ruled mini-table with Inspect at its lower edge. Composer is a simple ruled entry box; Send is a squared vermilion button. Strong original typographic identity, efficient and credible, no vintage textures or newspaper pastiche.
